attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing analytic input is a signed or scale-sharp bound for lambda_min(K_v^sing) and for T_tail(w) in four-dimensional Yang-Mills heat-kernel regulation, uniform enough for cutoff removal and obtained without assuming the target mass gap.
steps: Start from the locked finite Schur-Feshbach expansion of the same-theory Wilson quotient block. The rank-one vacuum direction and one-body Wilson factors have already been eliminated, leaving a positive null-channel margin M_G before irreducible endpoint terms.

Expand each Wilson loop in the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator. The product of the two second-order trace terms gives the color factor (g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 because N^{-1}tr(T^aT^b)=(T_F/N)delta^{ab}.

Separate the four-flux contribution into Wick-square pairings, the irreducible connected kappa_4 cumulant, and nonabelian commutator contacts. The Wick-square part is a positive Gram term, so it can only improve the null-channel lower bound.

Use the null incidence identity on the straight shared boundary segments to cancel the length-linear f f commutator contact. This is the cancellation that localizes the remaining danger to endpoint/corner boxes plus a tail.

For each endpoint v, view the singlet-projected connected four-flux cumulant as a self-adjoint finite regulated operator K_v^sing on symmetric two-flux tests. The null hairpin geometry inserts the specific test A_v(w)=sum_i w_i eta_i tensor_s eta_i.
Apply the spectral theorem: <A_v(w),K_v^sing A_v(w)> >= -Lambda_-(v)||A_v(w)||^2. Summing endpoints gives the displayed lower bound for the connected boundary-OPE polarization R.

Combine the endpoint bound with M_G. If M_eff remains positive, this block has no endpoint kappa_4 falsifier; if M_eff is negative with a realized endpoint eigenmode, the same-theory OS quotient determinant fails.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The reduction is valid finite-dimensional spectral algebra, but it has not computed the actual endpoint kappa_4 eigenvalue or proved a uniform endpoint-tail estimate for the Yang-Mills measure.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Endpoint-box kappa_4 spectral reduction for reflected Wilson hairpins

assumptions: Heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulation is reflection positive and has a gauge-invariant flux-source generating functional on each endpoint box.
The H,K Schur-Feshbach gate is already locked and supplies a strictly positive null-channel Gaussian margin M_G before the irreducible endpoint kappa_4 term is inserted.
The Wick-square four-flux contraction has been separated as a positive Gram contribution and is not used to create a falsifier.
The straight-segment nonabelian f f contact cancels by the null incidence identity for the actual three-hairpin geometry; only endpoint/corner boxes and tails remain.
Endpoint tails outside the chosen boxes admit a uniform same-theory bound T_tail(w) in the cutoff-removal regime.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated reflected Wilson hairpins C_i(delta,a,epsilon), endpoint boxes E_v(r), and null coefficient w=(1,1,-2).
target object: the same-theory OS quotient second-order scalar in the null channel after Schur-Feshbach elimination of the rank-one vacuum direction.
controlled interface: extract the connected boundary-OPE polarization R from plaquette flux cumulants and compare its endpoint negative spectrum with the positive Gaussian margin M_G.

same-theory condition: use the locked Wilson loop normalization, endpoint collaring, and cutoff-removal embedding; endpoint boxes localize the estimate but add no boundary counterterm or new observable.
kappa_4 endpoint operator: the real self-adjoint operator K_v^sing on symmetric color-singlet two-flux tests A supported in E_v, obtained from the connected four-flux cumulant.
negative spectral size: Lambda_-(v)=max(0,-lambda_min(K_v^sing)) in the endpoint-box test norm fixed by the heat-kernel plaquette covariance.
geometric incidence: A_v(w)=sum_i w_i eta_{i,v} tensor_s eta_{i,v} and I_v(w)=||A_v(w)||_HS^2, computed from the oriented plaquettes entering the endpoint of each hairpin.

equations.valid_when: Valid when the Wilson expansion is truncated to the connected four-flux endpoint term, with all four flux insertions supported inside one endpoint box.

equations.label: incidence norm
equations.valid_when: Applies once the oriented endpoint plaquette incidences are fixed by the locked Wilson collars before taking the continuum limit.

equations.label: endpoint negative-spectrum bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after the Wick-square Gram contraction is separated and the straight f f commutator contact cancels by the null incidence identity.

equations.valid_when: Valid when the corrected Schur-Feshbach H,K gate has already supplied a positive Gaussian margin M_G in the chosen null channel.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a regulated endpoint computation with an eigenvector overlapping A_v(w) for which the negative kappa_4 contribution plus tail exceeds M_G, or a failure of the straight f f cancellation in the actual oriented endpoint plaquette list.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma is the paper-handoff bridge from the concrete H,K hairpin block to a finite endpoint kappa_4 computation: it gives a valid promotion test and an explicit falsifier threshold without restating the Wilson/OS obstruction ladder.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the locked three-hairpin Wilson collar block, after the Wick-square Gram term and the straight f f contact are removed, the only post-H,K danger is the negative spectrum of a finite singlet-projected endpoint four-flux cumulant operator plus a tail. Thus R is reduced to a regulated endpoint eigenvalue estimate with an explicit color and incidence prefactor.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if endpoint localization fails, if the f f cancellation is not valid for the actual plaquette orientations, or if the cutoff topology cannot control T_tail(w).
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a regulated computation proves M_eff>0 uniformly as a,epsilon go to zero; demote to falsifier if M_eff<0 with a realized endpoint eigenmode overlapping A_v(w).
control_decision.reason: The branch has reduced the post-H,K obstruction to a computable endpoint-box eigenvalue and tail estimate with explicit color and incidence factors.

dependency_updates.description: Used only through the positive null-channel margin M_G and the corrected vacuum-direction Schur subtraction; no further obstruction-ladder restatement is needed.
Provides the null vector w and the cancellation identities for one-body, Wick-square-safe, and straight f f terms.
Need lambda_min(K_v^sing) or a rigorous upper bound on Lambda_-(v) in the heat-kernel plaquette endpoint box.
Need a same-theory bound on flux cumulants with at least one insertion outside endpoint boxes after the straight-contact cancellation.

falsifiers: A direct heat-kernel endpoint-box calculation gives (g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 sum_v Lambda_-(v)I_v(w)+|T_tail(w)| >= M_G with nonzero overlap on the hairpin incidence vector; this is a finite Wilson OS falsifier.
The oriented endpoint plaquette enumeration shows a residual straight-segment f f contact in the null channel, invalidating the localization used by the bound.
The connected four-flux cumulant has a boundary-scale nonlocal part that cannot be assigned to finitely many endpoint boxes with a valid uniform tail.
The endpoint estimate requires a boundary counterterm or a changed Wilson normalization, breaking the same-theory condition even if positivity is recovered in a modified algebra.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 245 turns the remaining R problem into a precise finite endpoint spectral estimate. The actual Yang-Mills object is the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet singlet connected four-flux cumulant K_v^sing. Wick-square terms are harmless Gram terms, and the straight f f contact cancels by the null incidence identity; the branch is not looping. Promotion or demotion now depends on the valid inequality comparing the negative endpoint kappa_4 spectrum and tail with M_G.
